cells.tense: Right now the bar is set where you can hold it, and you are holding it.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest version of the practice you keep postponing, do it today at full care, and stop when it is done.
cells.core:
You can carry weight without going rigid under it. That's a skill, not a mood, and it shows in how you take pressure — you steady, you don't stiffen, you don't fold. Shape gets kept. The strain gets admitted. The same thing holds in the small room where you repeat something until it takes: you can miss a day and come back without punishing yourself, which is the part most people can't do.

What this balance is free to feed next isn't more endurance. It's contact — letting someone stand close enough to see you while you carry it. Being seen without blurring into the other person, and without getting swallowed by them.
cells.sheetLine: You take the weight without stiffening, and without folding.
cells.verb: bearing what has to be carried without hardening or snapping
cells.place: the hour of repetitions, alone, where skill is built one session at a time

cells.tense: You are bracing for a break that has not come, and you are bracing hard.
cells.ask: Leave one thing slightly imperfect on purpose, and let it stand for the week.
cells.core:
You're gripping past the point the work asks for. There's a day coming when it all gives, and you're already living in that day, holding against it — so the practice stops being practice and becomes an exam you don't finish passing. Reps that were steadyness turn into a clamp. Rest reads as a hole in the record. The same grip spills past the room: you keep score in what you give and get until giving becomes a tab.

What pulls back is proportion — the plain sense of what's actually owed, from you and to you, without running the ledger every night. Most of what you're bracing against doesn't arrive. The load mostly holds itself.
cells.sheetLine: You're spending strength on a break that isn't coming.

cells.tense: Back then holding felt like standing unprotected, and part of you is still standing there.
cells.ask: Tell one person about something you stopped doing, then start it again this week — a few minutes, same spot, same hour.
cells.core:
The room where you used to keep something going is dark now. It isn't laziness and it isn't weakness — carrying anything landed as standing completely exposed, so you stopped putting anything in your hands. Effort feels risky before it even starts. Showing up gets postponed. What you were already carrying you still carry, quietly, without a practice and without saying so.

Pushing harder into the sore place won't open it; that's been tried. It opens sideways, by letting something end and setting it down on purpose. Small and finished. Then keeping something going is back where it was, and you can pick up one thing again.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped keeping anything, because holding it cost too much.

cells.tense: You are already building something by steady repetition, and you call it just getting through the days.
cells.ask: Notice one thing you did the same good way twice this week, and say out loud, once, that you made it happen.
cells.core:
There's a discipline running in you that you don't count as one. You show up to the same difficult thing again and again, you get a little better at it, and none of it goes in the record you keep about yourself. Either the showing-up reads as luck or as something anyone would do — or the other one, the part that goes flat when it matters, gets treated as the whole story about you, while the strength quietly holds. A practice is being built on a foundation of it isn't mine, isn't much, doesn't count.

Both stories take credit away from the same person. Nobody has to shine for this to be true — the practice grew. Saying so is just putting the pen back in your own hand.
cells.sheetLine: You built something steady and left your name off it.
cells.verb: bearing what has to be carried without hardening or snapping

attempts.check: The draft claims the person has been keeping some practice lit for a long time; the record only supports that the capacity for steady, repeatable effort exists, not its history or how it has actually gone for them. A reader could fairly say 'I haven't kept anything steady, I've just gotten through,' and the reading has no business overruling that. The ask survives being wrong either way — lowering the bar for one session and letting it stand done teaches the same thing whatever the read missed. The sentence that serves me and not them is any line about a flame or a light kept burning; it sounds earned and describes nobody.
